newsitem.title: DUBAI: Bahrain distances itself from businessmen in Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain distances itself from businessmen in Iraq.

text.p: Bahrain has distanced itself from a group of Bahraini businessmen visiting Iraq for the first time since the Gulf War and said they did not represent the Gulf Arab state's commercial sector.
"...The names that were mentioned (in press reports) have nothing to do with the business (community) in Bahrain," Information Minister Mohammad Ibrahim al-Mutawae said.
He told the London-based Arabic-language Asharq al-Awsat daily that Bahrain's Chamber of Commerce and Industry "represents the commercial sector and it has not sent a delegation to Iraq".
The Bahraini businessmen said in Baghdad on Wednesday they were seeking deals under an oil-for-food pact signed by Baghdad and the United Nations.

"We are here for business. We want to bring to Iraq foodstuffs and medicine allowed by the oil agreement with the United Nations," Abdul Ridha al-Kazrouni, one of the Bahraini businessmen, told Reuters.
He said they had met officials from the ministries of health, trade, transport and communications and industry to learn Iraq's needs of humanitarian goods.
Iraq's relations with Arab Gulf states have been strained since Baghdad's troops invaded Kuwait in 1990.
